corpusSummary: Across 2026 records, the corpus maps diverse social-science inquiries into large language models, spanning trust, embodiment, and ethics in human-AI interaction; AI as a research instrument for policy, climate, health, and education; assessment of safety, fairness, and misinformation; and the societal implications of AI-enabled decision making, pedagogy, and participation. The collection reveals recurring concerns about anthropomorphism, bias, dependency, and the need for governance and transparency.

themes.name: Human-AI interaction: trust, embodiment, and social dynamics
themes.description: Studies document how users perceive humanness and empathy, how devices influence well-being, and how adoption is shaped by social context, privacy, and trust in AI.

themes.name: AI as a research tool: methodological innovations, validation, and governance
themes.description: A broad set of papers demonstrates LLMs supporting data extraction, coding, simulations, and policy analysis, while emphasizing validation, transparency, and ethical oversight.

themes.name: AI in health, education, and well-being: safety, literacy, and equity
themes.description: Research assesses AI's role in health misinformation, clinical decision-making, AI-assisted education, and equity concerns in digital health governance.

themes.name: AI, misinformation, polarization, and governance in society
themes.description: There is a focus on misinformation, political persuasion, polarization, deepfakes, and governance frameworks for responsible AI deployment.
